sourceContract.serialAlias:
define serial http actor HttpActor as
end

semantics.requestConcurrency: maximum concurrent admitted HTTP request lifetimes per actor
semantics.messageConcurrency: maximum concurrent message lifetimes per request
semantics.actorExecution: at most one physical guest turn executing per actor incarnation
semantics.serial: exactly one admitted request lifetime and one message lifetime

cases.name: serial-alias
cases.oracle: The serial HTTP declaration and explicit (1,1) configuration lower to equivalent immutable HTTP actor policy metadata; aliases survive annotation expansion and tree shaking.

cases.name: nonserial-denial
cases.oracle: A (3,4) configuration may parse, but must fail with a compiler-owned unsupported capability diagnostic until runtime admission, state loans and guest reentry are implemented. Never silently clamp to (1,1).

cases.name: invalid-limits
cases.oracle: Zero, negative, nonliteral, duplicate and conflicting requestConcurrency/messageConcurrency declarations fail before any actor or socket is published.

cases.name: unbound-transport
cases.oracle: A generic mailbox spawn of an HTTP actor without a bound HTTP transport adapter fails closed; no silent ordinary actor fallback.

cases.name: two-level-lifetimes
cases.oracle: Request and per-request message lifetime reservations obey their separate limits; concurrent lifetimes never imply two physical executing guest turns on one actor incarnation.

cases.name: suspend-cancel-reentry
cases.oracle: Suspension holds logical admission while allowing carrier release; cancel/timeout releases reservations exactly once, prevents stale continuation reentry and keeps sealed-state loans exclusive.

cases.name: exchange-incarnation
cases.oracle: Request/exchange authority is one-shot and bound to exact scheduler domain, actor slot and incarnation plus exchange generation; stale, wrong actor, and double claims reject.

cases.name: shutdown-physical-exit
cases.oracle: Shutdown seals admission and rejects new requests, awaits accepted exchange and actor physical-turn quiescence, and does not claim success merely because socket response or mailbox drain completed.

cases.name: shutdown-failure
cases.oracle: If an actor remains physically active beyond deadline, shutdown returns explicit failure; retry/forced close does not double-finalize or report a false successful quiescence.

cases.name: demo-admission-restart
cases.oracle: The unchanged REST demo uses its single admitted request until actor completion, exposes explicit overload behavior, retains persisted state through normal restart and distinguishes termination from graceful draining.

cases.name: aot-provenance
cases.oracle: Each claimed backend compiles the unchanged canonical HTTP actor guest, executes real loopback HTTP, records exact source+compiler+artifact identity and verifies Native AOT/full-AOT where applicable.
